entry.title: From 21M to 65M ops/s: two changes to a C++ order book
entry.summary: Flat price-level arrays and an open-addressing id table took a C++20 order book from 20.9M to 65.2M ops/s; one step was slower first.

entry.title: Replaying 20 minutes of Binance BTCUSDT
entry.summary: 562,850 order operations: v2 at 79.4M ops/s against 14.7M for std::map, on a book of at most 4,203 orders, small enough to fit in cache. Speeds from the 30 October rerun at e12cc5d.

entry.title: v2: an open-addressing id table, and the 32 MB table that hid its gain
entry.summary: Sized for 1M orders the table didn't fit in cache; sized for the workload, v2 is 1.8× as fast as v1. Speeds from the 30 October reruns at e12cc5d and, for v1, 752c2cf.

entry.title: A benchmark found a full-band scan in my “faster” version
entry.summary: Clearing the last ask scanned all 65,536 ticks: 22.5 µs a sweep against 2.0 µs for std::map, as the benchmark timed it then.

entry.title: Apple Silicon’s steady_clock ticks every 41.7 ns
entry.summary: My p50 came out at exactly one tick of a 24 MHz clock.

entry.title: My first differential test passed with a planted bug in it
entry.summary: Queues never formed, so priority bugs had nothing to break.
